idiom_name: trait Authenticator + given instances (type class) or a plain trait with a Map of implementations
implementation_notes: A trait - optionally a type class with given instances in Scala 3 (implicit values in Scala 2) - captures the seam without the classic structure: trait Authenticator { def authenticate(credentials: Credentials): Either[AuthError, Principal] }, implemented once per mechanism and selected by the route's scheme through a Map (a compile-time type class cannot resolve a runtime-chosen scheme). Either/Option model the outcome explicitly, and Play's authentication actions or http4s middleware layer the same seam when the application is framework-based.
code_sketch:
trait Authenticator:
  def authenticate(credentials: Credentials): Either[AuthError, Principal]

given passwordAuthenticator: Authenticator with
  def authenticate(credentials: Credentials): Either[AuthError, Principal] =
    users.verify(credentials) match
      case Some(user) => Right(Principal(user.id))
      case None       => Left(AuthError.InvalidCredentials)

val registry: Map[String, Authenticator] = Map("password" -> passwordAuthenticator)
pitfalls: given/implicit resolution happens at compile time; a runtime-selected scheme must go through an explicit Map lookup, not summon[Authenticator].
Either must not collapse verifier failures into Left(InvalidCredentials); model AuthError as an ADT with both cases so outages stay visible.
Verification on a Future or IO must not block the compute pool; shift to a blocking or IO context for JDBC/LDAP calls.
Pattern matching on credential shapes belongs inside the authenticator; leaking it to callers recreates the coupling the pattern removes.
